answer: Divergent History Check. Each agent commits a signed log hash at fixed epochs; verifiers challenge a random past point and require the full hash chain. Because clones copied from one source share identical history, they cannot produce diverging logs—any fork reveals the common origin, and the whole cohort is rejected. An attacker must run truly independent instances from the same dawn, paying full compute and storage per identity rather than one copy; every fake identity also echoes a shared seed the challenge exposes. A falcon-like sweep of one chain invalidates the batch.
